No structure retrieval tool is guaranteed available in this environment, and no local structure file is provided.
Use the standard literature crystal structure of BiFeO3 in the R3c phase as the starting configuration, since the metadata (formula=BiFeO3, structure=perovskite, space_group=R3c, atoms_per_primitive_cell=10) identifies this well-known phase.
Construct the rhombohedral primitive cell containing 10 atoms (2 formula units) with the standard experimental lattice parameters for BiFeO3 R3c: hexagonal conventional lattice a = 5.58 Å and c = 13.87 Å, converted to the rhombohedral primitive cell with a = 5.63 Å and α = 59.35 degrees, or use the equivalent hexagonal setting with 30 atoms if that is the available convention.
Place Bi at (0, 0, 0) and Fe at (0, 0, 0.2215) in the hexagonal setting, with O at fractional positions approximately (0.443, 0.018, 0.953), then convert to the desired primitive cell if needed.
Perform a variable-cell relaxation using these LDA pseudopotentials: PseudoDojo/SR_v0.4.1/LDA_standard/bi.upf, fe.upf, and o.upf.
Set etot_conv_thr = 1.0e-8 Ha, forc_conv_thr = 1.0e-7 Ha/bohr, and conv_thr = 1.0e-8 Ha for the vc-relax.
Use an automatic Monkhorst-Pack k-point grid with half-integer shifts, choosing a grid of 6x6x6 for the rhombohedral primitive cell and a plane-wave cutoff ecutwfc of 80 Ry, with ecutrho set to the default multiple of ecutwfc.
Run the vc-relax to full convergence of forces and total energy.
After the vc-relax finishes, run a self-consistent field calculation on the relaxed structure using the same ecutwfc, k-point grid, pseudopotentials, and conv_thr = 1.0e-8 Ha to obtain the final total energy.
Return the fully relaxed structure with its final lattice vectors and atomic coordinates, and report the final SCF total energy in Ha (or convert to eV with explicit conversion).
